instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We wanted somewhere to belong. This leaking cottage can still be ours. Start at the roof, the way I taught you to inspect a place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole roof needs replacing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked past the paint this time. Good. We'll know every tile of the house we belong in. Help me measure it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That roof could take all our savings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then those savings become the roof over us. I taught you to put money aside for a home; here it is. Write down the cost, and let's decide how much of that roof we can lay ourselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We said this concert would bring the village together. Give the first note the way I taught you; let them hear where to join.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The power's out. Nobody can hear the microphone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You checked before singing, at least. Put the microphone down and bring the front row closer. We'll sing together instead of making them listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Half of them have gone home for torches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they'll bring the light as well as their voices. Leave room for them in the circle, like I showed you with new singers. Ask the ones still here to start the chorus.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my good teacup home. I taught you to warm it first, remember? I'd like our afternoons to go with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are you talking as if I won't come back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can make a proper pot without me now, at last. Take the matching saucer too; you'll have everything you need when I'm not here to fuss.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you asking me to leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, love. Sit for one last cup from my pot. Hold it by the handle, as I showed you, and let me pour while that's still my job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed extra sandwiches for your journey. You remember how I taught you to wrap them separately so you could save one for later?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm only visiting the next town.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered the route without asking me this time. Take the flask too, sweetheart; then you can stay as long as you need.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That sounds very final.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then come here before you go. Let me tuck a napkin beside the last sandwich, the way I always did for you. Promise you'll eat that sandwich even when I'm not there to remind you.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift costs petrol and an answer about why you stopped calling. I taught you to keep a promise even when the conversation was awkward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay for petrol.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're offering without being chased now. Good. That pays for the drive. I still need you to tell me why my calls went unanswered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we talk another day?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the petrol money ready. Now I also need to hear why one more day of waiting is fair to me. Use the full answer I taught you, not another date you might forget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrow the dress for ten pounds and admit you mocked it. I taught you to judge the cut before sneering at the colour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can count the price, at least. Keep the extra ten. It doesn't tell me what happened to your 'dreadful taste' remark.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. It's beautiful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ten pounds, and tell the people you said it to who chose it. You used to need me to finish every seam; now you can finish that compliment where they can hear it.

cards.title: Agree to the Exact Words
cards.instruction: Agree to the exact wording, then use later callbacks to narrow what those words can obligate you to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll carry one box. Count before you start loading, the way I taught you on your first move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to help me move the whole storeroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've remembered the help, at least. Now read the rest: one box. Put one by the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The biggest one, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Label it 'one' before I lift it, just as I showed you. Once that box is in the van, don't put another under the same label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I agree to watch your dog today. Write the day on the rota, the way I taught you when you first got him.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow's only a few hours away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You checked the clock this time. Good. A few hours is what remains of 'today'; your name goes in tomorrow's square.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you loved dogs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I do. I'll pack his favourite blanket for you to take home tonight. Read my square again, like we practised: today. Bring his lead before midnight.

cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said nothing could go wrong and balanced the hall key on my teacup. I taught you to put keys with the invitation, away from drinks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fell in. I used the invitation to dry it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered to dry the key, at least. Now the hall address has run into a tea stain. That was our only copy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The key still works. We can scrape the paper off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then scrape it, and ring the bride. Start with good news, as I taught you: 'The key still works.' Then tell her what the tea did to our only copy of the address and ask where to bring it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called the spare chair unnecessary, then put the cake on it. I taught you to count seats before finding somewhere for the food.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake needed a flat surface.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You found one without tilting the cake this time. Now the extra guest has taken the piano stool, and the pianist has nowhere to sit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can have your chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Take it to the piano, then cut me a slice from the chair we didn't need. I taught you to serve the host last; today you can serve your teacher standing up.
